text_blocks.snippet: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) causes high blood pressure in the arteries of your lungs, leading to symptoms that start mild during exercise and worsen over time even at rest.
snippet_highlighted_words: start mild during exercise and worsen over time even at rest

list.snippet: Shortness of breath: Usually starts during physical activity (like climbing stairs) and can eventually happen while resting.
Fatigue and weakness: Feeling very tired or lacking energy to complete normal daily tasks.
Chest pain or pressure: Caused by the extra strain placed on the heart as it works harder to pump blood.
Dizziness or fainting: Lightheadedness or fainting spells (syncope), especially during physical exertion.
Swelling (Edema): Fluid buildup in the ankles, feet, legs, or belly area as the heart struggles.
Heart palpitations: A racing, pounding, or skipping heartbeat.
Bluish skin, lips, or fingers: Known as cyanosis, caused by a lack of sufficient oxygen in the blood.

text_blocks.snippet: You can learn more detailed information about warning signs from the American Lung Association or read the Mayo Clinic Guide on Pulmonary Hypertension.
